Alex / Marissa — notes from the technical/pricing perspective below. Long story short: we can meet p95 ~200–300ms with Hosted Pro for smaller volumes, but for predictable costs at 60M+/mo and bursty spikes we recommend evaluating Dedicated (reserved) paths.

Option summary (high level):
1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go) — fast to start, simple.
   - Pros: no commitment, instant provisioning, streaming enabled by default.
   - Cons: higher unit $/1M tokens (we estimate ~ $400–600 / 1M for the model profile you described), variability during bursts.

2) Hosted + SLO overlay (premium) — keep hosted API but purchase an SLO overlay for tighter p95 guarantees.
   - Pros: short time to value and SLA-backed latency tiers.
   - Cons: extra overlay fee (adds to $/1M). Good if you want no infra changes.

3) Dedicated reserved pool — recommended if monthly committed volume > ~40–50M tokens and you need predictable unit economics and control over batching.
   - Pros: lower unit cost (we can get to ~$220–300 / 1M with a 6–12 month commit depending on exact commit size), configurable batch windows, predictable tail-latency with warm workers.
   - Cons: provisioning lead time and minimum commit.

Batching vs streaming notes: 
- Batching (larger batch sizes) reduces per-token GPU overhead and cuts unit cost, but it increases latency variance. For interactive flows we suggest conservative batching windows (20–50ms) — yields decent cost savings while keeping p95 in your 200–300ms band.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for users (chunks arrive as generated). It adds minimal cost for network/encoding and can slightly increase compute overhead, but it’s generally the best UX for chat without materially increasing token cost.

Cache and warm-KV: 
- If you have high prefix reuse (templated prompts), prefix/KV caching can dramatically reduce tokens billed and the effective cost. We should quantify this in the pilot.

SLO-driven pricing (example):
- Base hosted price: ~$400 / 1M tokens
- Low-latency overlay (p95 < 150ms): +25–40% premium
- Dedicated (reserved) price: ~$220 / 1M tokens (with 6–12m commit)

Attachments I’m adding: redwood-pricing-vs-latency.pdf (matrix + example math), and a short demo recording for how streaming looks in the console (demo-recording.mp4). I’ll also include a worked example with your forecast numbers if you confirm the XLS.

If you want, we can run a 2-week dedicated trial (no long-term commit) where we:
- provision a small reserved pool for your peak-critical flows,
- run a set of 3 prompts / 2k tokens each through streaming vs batched runs, and
- report back on measured p95 and effective $/1M.

Happy to jump on a quick technical call to design the pilot — propose Wed 3/24 10:00am PT.
